items.followUp: Why is ROM called non-volatile memory?

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying RAM as volatile.

rubric.why: Explains that RAM does not retain its data without power.
rubric.description: States that stored data is lost when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the data is lost when power is removed.

modelAnswer: RAM is called volatile memory because it stores data temporarily.
Its contents are lost when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: What is a proposition in logic?

rubric.why: Identifies a proposition as a statement or declarative sentence.
rubric.description: Defines a proposition as a statement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a statement or declarative sentence.

rubric.why: States the defining feature that a proposition has a truth value.
rubric.description: Says that it can be judged true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning its truth value.

modelAnswer: A proposition is a declarative statement that expresses an idea.
It has a truth value: it is either true or false.

items.followUp: Name two common threats to data security.

rubric.description: Identifies one issue related to data security.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming one valid issue, such as unauthorized access, hacking, a virus, or data loss.

rubric.why: Gives a second valid data-security issue.
rubric.description: Identifies a second issue related to data security.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a different valid issue.

modelAnswer: Two issues related to data security are unauthorized access and data loss.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a proxy server?

rubric.why: Identifies the proxy as an intermediary server.
rubric.description: States that a proxy is an intermediary server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a server that acts as an intermediary.

rubric.why: Describes how a proxy handles communication on behalf of a client.
rubric.description: States that it receives or forwards client requests to another server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning client requests and their forwarding or handling.

modelAnswer: A proxy is an intermediary server between a client and another server.
It receives and forwards requests on behalf of the client.

items.followUp: What is file sharing over a network?

rubric.why: Identifies the item being shared as an application or software.
rubric.description: States that an application or software is shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the application or software.

rubric.why: Explains that users can share or access the application.
rubric.description: States that users can use or access the shared application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that users share, access, or use it.

modelAnswer: Application sharing allows users to share an application over a network.
Users can access and use the shared application.

items.followUp: What is a receiver in a communication system?

rubric.why: Identifies a message as the information or data being communicated.
rubric.description: States that a message is information or data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message as information or data.

rubric.why: Connects the message to its role in communication.
rubric.description: States that the message is sent from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the information is communicated between sender and receiver.

modelAnswer: A message is the information or data communicated in a communication system.
It is sent from a sender to a receiver.

items.followUp: What is the function of the Transport Layer?

rubric.why: Identifies logical addressing as a Network Layer function.
rubric.description: States that the Network Layer provides logical addressing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning logical or IP addressing.

rubric.why: Identifies routing or packet forwarding as a Network Layer function.
rubric.description: States that it routes or forwards packets between networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning routing or packet forwarding between networks.

modelAnswer: The Network Layer provides logical addressing, such as IP addresses.
It routes and forwards packets from one network to another.

items.followUp: What is HTTPS, and what is it used for?

rubric.description: Expands HTTP as Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct expansion.

rubric.why: Describes HTTP's role in transferring web resources.
rubric.description: States that it transfers web pages or other web resources between a browser and a web server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the transfer of web content between a browser and a server.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
It is used to transfer web pages and other web resources between a browser and a web server.
